sections.h2: Where is the Town of Babylon, and which villages and hamlets are inside it?
sections.html:
One of Suffolk County's ten towns, Babylon fronts the Atlantic on Long Island's south shore. Nassau County is its western neighbor, Huntington lies north and Islip lies east. The western boundary sits roughly 20 miles from the Queens line.

Three incorporated villages and a long list of hamlets share the town, so an address can follow different local rules than the town name suggests.

  • Villages: Amityville in the southwest, Lindenhurst in the south and Babylon in the southeast
  • Hamlets: Copiague, Deer Park, East Farmingdale, North Amityville, North Babylon, North Lindenhurst, West Babylon, Wheatley Heights and Wyandanch
  • Barrier-island communities: Gilgo, Oak Beach, Captree and part of Fire Island west of the Robert Moses Causeway

Town Hall stands on East Sunrise Highway in Lindenhurst. For a house inside one of the villages, ask the village office what it adds on top of the town's taxes and permits.

sections.h2: How did Babylon grow into a town of 219,766 people?
sections.html:
The area was once called Huntington South. Around 1803 the families who settled there named it New Babylon, and in 1872 it became its own town, divided from Huntington.

The postwar decades were the big ones. Census counts went from 45,556 in 1950 to 142,309 in 1960 and 204,256 in 1970. Babylon has stayed above 200,000 since and reached 218,223 in 2020. Houses from that boom are decades old now, so a buyer will ask how old the roof and heating system are.

Know whether your address is in a village or a hamlet, because buyers compare areas closely.

sections.h2: How expensive is housing in Babylon by Census measures?
sections.html:
Owners live in 78.3% of Babylon's homes, and a typical owned home is valued at $522,100. Owners with a mortgage report monthly costs near $3,206.

Households average 3.13 people, well above the national 2.53, and 93.5% of residents had the same address a year earlier. With owner costs that high, the tax bill gets close attention from buyers.

sections.h2: How do the railroad and airports shape Babylon buyers' choices?
sections.html:
The Long Island Rail Road's Babylon Branch is the principal line, with stops from Amityville to Babylon village. The Main Line passes through the northern hamlets, serving Pinelawn, Wyandanch and Deer Park. Suffolk County Transit buses cover most of the rest.

Republic Airport in East Farmingdale houses the American Airpower Museum, and Long Island MacArthur Airport in Ronkonkoma, nearby, has commercial flights. Workers here average a 31.0 minute commute, against 26.4 nationally.

Distance to a station is worth stating. Say which station is closest when you describe the house.

sections.h2: What does the Great South Bay shoreline mean for a Babylon house?
sections.html:
Water makes up over half of the town's 114 square miles, and its elevation averages about 6.6 feet. The Great South Bay, Fire Island Inlet and Atlantic beaches form the southern line. Town parks include Southard's Pond Park in the village and Tanner Park in Copiague, and state parks include Belmont Lake, Captree and Robert Moses.

Low ground and open water shape insurance, repairs and buyer questions. Ask your insurance agent whether your house sits in a flood zone before you list.

Sewer billing shifted in 2026. On January 1 all Suffolk County sewer districts merged into the Suffolk County Wastewater Management District, which may have changed your rate or billing method. Check the sewer line on your tax bill.

sections.h2: What is the Babylon tax calendar, and what do late payments cost?
sections.html:
Babylon's tax year starts December 1 and ends November 30, with one bill mailed around mid-December. An owner may pay it whole or in halves. For 2025-26, the first half fell due in the second week of January 2026 and the second half at the end of May, and both have passed. The next bill is due to arrive in mid-December.

  • A first half paid late grows by 1% for each month, topping out at 5% in mid to late May.
  • Once May ends, unpaid taxes are delinquent and go to the Suffolk County Comptroller in Riverhead, with a 5% penalty and 1% monthly interest running from February 1.
  • The office takes partial payments starting at $200.
  • Cards online add a 2.35% fee and e-checks add $1.
  • If a balance is still open at the tax lien sale, usually in December, the county sells a lien on the property.

The Receiver of Taxes collects but does not set rates. School, county and town budgets decide the amounts, and school tax is usually the biggest line. A missing bill is no excuse for a late payment.

sections.h2: How can a Babylon owner pay a tax bill, and who else can receive a copy?
sections.html:
Taxes can be paid online through the payment processor, by mail with a detached stub, or at Town Hall in the main hallway. In person, the office takes cash and checks but not cards, and a drop box accepts checks during business hours. Mailed payments are credited on the postmark date, and a metered postmark does not count.

An owner who is 65 or older, or disabled, and who lives in a one, two or three-family home may name a consenting adult to receive duplicate bills and notices of unpaid taxes. That application is due by October 1. For a parent's house you are about to sell, it is worth asking whether such a notice was ever set up.

sections.h2: Which exemptions and assessment deadlines affect a Babylon sale?
sections.html:
Babylon's Department of Assessment takes exemption applications until March 1 and denies late ones. The list includes Enhanced STAR, Aged, Alternative Veterans, Cold War Veterans, volunteer firefighter and ambulance worker, disability with limited income, Capital Improvement and first-time buyer of a newly built home. Newcomers to Basic STAR get a state credit in place of a school tax exemption.

One point matters at sale: an exemption follows the person who qualified. If your house carries a senior or veteran exemption, the buyer should expect it to end, and the tax bill could climb. Tell the buyer early.

Complaints about an assessment use Form RP-524. Suffolk County's town review boards sit on the third Tuesday in May, which is May 18 in 2027. The town builds values from square footage and amenities.

sections.h2: What happens at a Babylon closing, and where does a cash offer fit?
sections.html:
New York's transfer tax, two dollars for each $500 of price, is normally the seller's expense. The Suffolk County Clerk files the TP-584 return, and payment is due 15 days after the deed is delivered.

Third-party payers such as banks, title companies and attorneys pay a $1 duplicate tax bill fee, sent as a separate check. Plan for that when a title company clears your open tax bill at closing.

A listed sale follows the buyer's mortgage schedule. A cash purchase takes the house as it is and can close on your timeline, which suits deferred repairs, an overdue tax balance or an estate. In both cases, line up the deed, the latest tax statement and a lender payoff.

faqs.q: When do Babylon tax payments come due?
faqs.a: Bills mail in mid-December. Half is due in the second week of January and half at the end of May, and a late first half gains 1% a month.

faqs.q: Where do Babylon taxes go after May 31?
faqs.a: They go to the Suffolk County Comptroller's Office in Riverhead, carrying a 5% penalty and 1% monthly interest counted from February 1.

faqs.q: Does my STAR or senior exemption pass to the buyer in Babylon?
faqs.a: No. A new owner applies separately, and the tax bill may rise. The application deadline is March 1.

faqs.q: Do Babylon sellers owe a transfer tax?
faqs.a: Yes, the state charges two dollars per $500 of price, usually paid by the seller, with the TP-584 filed at the Suffolk County Clerk 15 days after the deed.

faqs.q: When must a Babylon assessment complaint be filed?
faqs.a: Suffolk County's town boards meet on the third Tuesday in May. The form is RP-524, and filing costs nothing.
